Question: Let the set consisting of the squares of the positive integers be called \(u;\) thus \(u\) is the set \(1,\) \(4,\) \(9,\) \(\ldots.\) If a certain operation on one or more members of the set always yields a member of the set, we say that the set is closed under that operation. Then \(u\) is closed under:

Choices.D: extraction of a positive integral root

Solution:
Closure requires every allowed input to produce an output in the set. Let \(m^2\) and \(n^2\) be any two members of \(u\), where \(m,n\) are positive integers. Then
\[
m^2n^2=(mn)^2.
\]
Since \(mn\) is a positive integer, this product belongs to \(u\). Repeating the argument proves the same for any finite product.

One counterexample rules out each other operation. Addition fails because \(1+1=2\) is not an integer square. Division fails because \(1\div4=\tfrac14\) is not an integer square. Root extraction fails because \(\sqrt4=2\) is not an integer square, even though \(4\) belongs to \(u\).

Thus \(u\) is closed under multiplication, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
